desc: Implement a sliding-window median structure using two heaps (max-heap for lower half, min-heap for upper half) with lazy deletion via a hash map, maintaining running sums of both halves so the absolute-deviation cost can be derived in O(1).
Compute cost[i] for every window starting at i (0 <= i <= n-x): cost = median*size_low - sum_low + sum_high - median*size_high, handling even/odd x correctly.
Implement the DP: dp[j][i] over j in 1..k and window indices, using dp[j][i] = min(dp[j][i-1], dp[j-1][i-x] + cost[i]); use rolling arrays with a large sentinel for impossible states.
Verify the solution on the two provided examples (expect 8 and 3).
Test edge cases: x = n (single window, k=1), all elements already equal (cost 0), negative numbers, and k*x = n (forced partition), plus a brute-force cross-check on small random inputs.
